title: Backward sweep updates one tape block
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes, let $\alpha$ be a one-step action, and let $j\in\mathbb{Z}$. Apply the backward-sweep rule successively to the reversed block encoding the tape cells at coordinate $j$, with the recorded neighboring head flags, starting from the head-flag table at coordinate $j+1$. The result is the head-flag table at coordinate $j$ together with the reversed block encoding at coordinate $j$ of the configuration obtained by applying $\alpha$ to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes
$\alpha$ is an action for that machine
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine, $\alpha$ an action of that
machine, and $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. Folding the backward-sweep visit rule for $\alpha$ over
the reversed block encoding coordinate $j$ (with recorded left-neighbour flags),
starting from the table of head flags at coordinate $j+1$, yields the table of head
flags at coordinate $j$ together with the reversed block encoding coordinate $j$ of the
configuration obtained by applying $\alpha$ to $c$.
